sentences.text: Mature individuals of this animal show significant size variation, weighing between 6.4 kg and over 15.4 kg.
The holotype specimen, which serves as the standard reference for the species, preserves parts of the skull, vertebrae, and the left front and hind legs.
Its well-developed optic lobe suggests it relied heavily on sight rather than smell to hunt.
Unlike many modern reptiles, its bones were not pneumatized and lacked an invasive air sac system.
The holotype specimen ULBRA-PVT280 was discovered in 2009 at the Buriol ravine in São João do Polêsine, Brazil.
The genus name Buriolestes was coined in 2016 by the Buriol family, combining their surname with the Greek word for 'robber' or 'thief'.
The specific name schultzi honors the paleontologist Cezar Schultz.
The shape of its teeth indicates it fed on small vertebrates and invertebrates.
A 2020 study noted that its brain morphology was similar to that of crocodiles.
The association of Buriolestes and Ixalerpeton recalls the simultaneous presence of dinosaurian and non-dinosaurian dinosauromorphs at other sites.
A phylogenetic analysis published in 2016 confirmed its affinities with sauropodomorphs, placing it within the class Saurischia.
Buriolestes lived during the Late Triassic in the Paraná Basin of southern Brazil, specifically within the Santa Maria Formation of the Carnian age, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Other analyses based on the original dataset place Buriolestes as the single most basal sauropodomorph.
